questions.stem: Which of the following gases is most soluble in water?
questions.solution:
Among the given gases, carbon dioxide is the most soluble in water. This is due to its ability to react with water to form carbonic acid:
$$\mathrm{CO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow H_2CO_3}$$
This reaction increases its solubility significantly compared to other gases like oxygen, nitrogen, and hydrogen, which are relatively non-reactive and only physically dissolve in water.
Quick Tip: Carbon dioxide's solubility is higher because it forms carbonic acid when dissolved in water, unlike other gases that only dissolve physically.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements does not have a completely filled outermost shell in its ground state?
questions.solution:
Neon, Helium, and Argon are noble gases with completely filled outermost electron shells in their ground states. Oxygen, on the other hand, has the electron configuration $1s^{2}\,2s^{2}\,2p^{4}$, meaning it has only 6 electrons in its outermost shell (which can hold up to 8). Thus, it does not have a completely filled outer shell.
Quick Tip: Noble gases like He, Ne, and Ar have completely filled valence shells. Elements like oxygen do not, making them more chemically reactive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a redox reaction?
questions.solution:
A redox reaction is a chemical reaction involving both reduction and oxidation. In the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide ($\mathrm{H_2O_2}$), oxygen is reduced (from $-1$ in $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ to $-2$ in $\mathrm{H_2O}$) and simultaneously oxidized (from $-1$ to $0$ in $\mathrm{O_2}$). Hence, it is a redox reaction.
Quick Tip: In redox reactions, always look for changes in oxidation numbers to identify which species are oxidized and reduced.

questions.stem: In the reaction $\mathrm{2H_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O}$, if 4 moles of hydrogen react completely with oxygen, how many moles of water will be produced?
questions.solution:
From the balanced equation:
$$\mathrm{2H_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O}$$
2 moles of hydrogen produce 2 moles of water. So, 4 moles of hydrogen will produce:
$$\frac{2\ \mathrm{mol\ H_2O}}{2\ \mathrm{mol\ H_2}} \times 4\ \mathrm{mol\ H_2} = 4\ \mathrm{mol\ H_2O}$$
Quick Tip: Always use the mole ratio from the balanced chemical equation to solve stoichiometry problems.

questions.stem: What is the volume of oxygen required for complete combustion of 0.25 mole of methane at S.T.P.?
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the combustion of methane is:
$$\mathrm{CH_4 + 2O_2 \rightarrow CO_2 + 2H_2O}$$
This shows 1 mole of methane requires 2 moles of oxygen for complete combustion.
At S.T.P., 1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 L. So, 2 moles of oxygen occupy:
$$2 \times 22.4 = 44.8\ \mathrm{L}$$
Therefore, for 0.25 moles of methane, the volume of oxygen required is:
$$0.25 \times 44.8 = 11.2\ \mathrm{L}$$
Quick Tip: Use the mole ratio from the balanced equation and remember that 1 mole of gas at STP occupies 22.4 L.
